items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: And at the time, World War I, when the government took the railroad over, he was so upset with the way they were handling things that he resigned, and he went in with W. C. Durant, who was an automobile manufacturer.

ctx.x: And it was your maternal grandfather who was connected with the railroad, is that right?

Yes. He started out in life as a telegraph operator, in I believe it was Lima, Ohio, and he went on up the ladder there and finally became executive first vice president of the Grand Central -- I mean the New York Central Railroad. And at the time, World War I, when the government took the railroad over, he was so upset with the way they were handling things that he resigned, and he went in with W. C. Durant, who was an automobile manufacturer. He had -- well, they made the Durant, they made the Locomobile, they…
into this void and was more or less of a father to me.
